title: Textron Delivers 500th CJ4 Article
notes:
Concept: LinkedIn post drawn from a third-party article. NOT a reprint — 
this is VJS's read on what the article means for people who fly privately. 
Do not reproduce the article's sentences, headline structure, or its 
sequence of points. Do not quote more than one short phrase, and only if 
the exact wording matters. Do not present the article's reporting as VJS's 
own findings.

Source: [article title, publication, URL]

Angle: [What VJS actually thinks about this. The post exists because we 
have a point of view on the news — not because the news happened. If we 
have nothing to add beyond "this happened," don't post it.]

Themes to hit:
- The one fact from the article that matters most to our audience — stated 
  in our own words, attributed to the publication
- Why it matters to someone weighing charter, fractional, or ownership
- What it doesn't mean — the overread we want to head off
- [Optional: what we're seeing on our side that supports or complicates it]

Attribution: Name the publication in the body. Link in the first comment, 
not the post. Never imply VJS conducted the research.

Closing message: The takeaway is a judgment, not a summary. Someone who 
read the article should still get something from this post.

CTA: [e.g. "If you're rethinking how you fly this year, we'll walk you 
through the tradeoffs."]

Tone: Confident and warm, not breathless. Informed peer, not commentator. 
No "thoughts?" fishing, no "this is huge," no exclamation points. First 
person singular where a named person is posting; first person plural for 
the company page.

Length: 900-1,300 characters. Hook lands in the first 140.

Compliance: No prices, no tail numbers, no availability claims, no implied 
endorsement by the publication or anyone quoted in it.

Turned into posts (2026-08-18): 2026-08-18-li-cj4-milestone-what-it-means.
